chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen, and when he arrived, he said to him: 'Tell me of the most surprising thing that has happened to you.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a group of men came to me who had purchased a female slave, and they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity, and she gave birth to a boy. They disputed over him, and each claimed him. So I cast lots among them, and gave him to the one whose lot was drawn, and I guaranteed him their share. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not the case with a group of people who dispute and then entrust their matter to Allah, except that the lot of the rightful one will emerge.'

key_terms.تَبَايَعُوا: They purchased (each other's share or jointly)
key_terms.طُهْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: A single period of purity (between menstruations)

ai.seo_question: How did Ali ibn Abi Talib resolve a paternity dispute among multiple men who had intercourse with the same slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib’s judicial wisdom in Yemen, where he resolved a complex paternity dispute among multiple men who had intercourse with a slave girl in one period of purity by casting lots (*kura*). The Prophet Muhammad affirmed this method, establishing the principle that when multiple claimants exist and evidence is equal, entrusting the decision to Allah through lots reveals the rightful owner (*al-muḥiqq*). This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for cases of *shubha* (doubt) regarding lineage, emphasizing that the lot does not create ownership but reveals the pre-existing right.
